articles.title: US House committee report found systemic antisemitism, lack of response to concerns within APA
articles.body:
A congressional investigation by the House Committee on Education and the Workforce concluded that the American Psychological Association (APA) has been co-opted by radical activists who promoted ideology demonizing Israel and allowed systemic antisemitism to spread within the organization, according to a recent report.
The APA leadership rejected the report’s conclusions, stating that the association unequivocally condemns antisemitism and has taken concrete steps to address concerns raised by Jewish mental health professionals.
The congressional inquiry was officially launched in December 2025 under Chairman Tim Walberg, following mounting complaints from Jewish members who alleged that antisemitic rhetoric and discrimination were being permitted across the association’s governance, publications, listservs, and annual conventions. The committee examined thousands of internal emails, drafts, and administrative records to evaluate how the nation’s leading professional organization for psychologists handled anti-Jewish bias.
The report, titled “Antisemitism at the American Psychological Association,” says that APA leadership systematically appeased anti-Israel affiliate groups while ignoring, dismissing, or mocking Jewish members who raised concerns.
The findings highlight internal deliberations surrounding the APA’s public statement following the October 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attacks in Israel. According to internal communications, APA leaders consulted with an affiliate group, the American Arab, Middle Eastern, and North African Psychological Association (AMENA-Psy), whose leaders urged the association to remove references to terrorism. Incoming AMENA-Psy leadership argued that “terrorist attacks need to change” and claimed the term was “one-sided and overused with Arabs,” while an internal APA draft attempted to equate Hamas attacks with Israeli military responses.
The final public statement released by the APA omitted any mention of terrorism.
Concerns from Jewish members were dismissed
The report also detailed internal emails written by senior APA figures in the weeks after the attack. Internal messages revealed that 2024 APA President Cynthia de las Fuentes compared Hamas’s attack on Israelis to the murder of George Floyd, writing that police officers are equivalent to “believers of ‘by any means necessary’ in achieving the goals of Zionism, similar to other terrorist groups’ missions,” while claiming “George Floyd is representative of Gazans.”
Further internal records documented leadership’s handling of complaints. When Jewish psychologists wrote to the association expressing distress over rising antisemitism, the APA’s chief diversity officer internally responded, “Sigh!” while another senior official complained about “the Jews who are so angry at us,” accusing them of “feeding hatred” by raising concerns publicly. The report noted that the APA declined to complete an Anti-Defamation League (ADL) survey regarding antisemitism, with staff claiming the questionnaire was “clearly aimed at finding fault” with the association.
Across governance and professional standards, the committee found that anti-Zionist members successfully altered the APA’s resolution on antisemitism in February 2026. The Council of Representatives voted 127-37 to adopt a revised resolution that introduced clauses regarding the “weaponization of antisemitism” and relied on the Jerusalem Declaration on Antisemitism over the objections of an internal Jewish advisory group.
Additionally, ethnic minority psychological associations within the APA mobilized against a resolution to recognize a Jewish ethnic psychological association, with opponents arguing that Jews benefit from “white privilege” and do not face the same structural oppression as non-white minorities.
The investigation also highlighted how division listservs, newsletters, and academic publications were used to circulate extreme rhetoric. Listserv posts by members defended Hamas’s actions as “resistance,” described Israel as a “terrorist” state, and dismissed concerns that Hamas sought to exterminate Jews as “quite hilarious”. In 2025, the flagship journal American Psychologist published an article referencing “Palestinian freedom fighters” and pathologizing “Zionist psychologies,” leading an editor of a planned special issue on antisemitism to resign over what he called “incendiary, politicized” content lacking scholarly rigor.
In its conclusion, the committee warned that the politicization of the APA threatens the credibility of the entire mental health field and noted that the Department of Education’s accreditation advisory panel recently recommended a one-year suspension of the APA’s accrediting commission. The report stated that the committee’s findings will inform upcoming legislative efforts targeting discrimination by accrediting bodies to ensure equal treatment and professional integrity.
Senior APA officials claimed report was inaccurate
In an internal email to colleagues obtained and reported by the Jewish News Syndicate (JNS), APA President Wendi S. Williams and CEO Arthur C. Evans, Jr. reportedly rejected the committee’s findings.
“We don’t agree with this report,” Williams and Evans wrote, stating that “the American Psychological Association unequivocally condemns antisemitism in all its forms.”
APA leadership maintained in the message that the organization has actively worked to address internal concerns, including holding listening sessions with Jewish psychologists.
“We recognize that this work requires continued attention and action, and we remain committed to advancing APA’s mission to promote well-being and respect for all,” Williams and Evans added.
ADL condemns APA's response to the report
Following the report’s release, the ADL issued a statement commending the House committee’s investigation and criticizing the APA’s response.
“Antisemitism at the American Psychological Association is not isolated,” the ADL stated. “It is embedded in its ranks and in its leadership.”
The ADL noted that Jewish groups had repeatedly warned APA leadership about escalating bias over the past year without seeing adequate institutional action.
“When a healing profession treats one group’s pain with such indifference, Jewish patients are right to wonder whether they will be met with compassion or with contempt,” the ADL added, calling on the APA to conduct an independent investigation, strengthen accountability measures, and mandate antisemitism training for its leadership.
The Jerusalem Post reached out to the House Committee on Education and the Workforce and the American Psychological Association for comment on Sunday, but did not receive a response prior to publication.

articles.title: Pope Leo says he hopes Oleshky truce could spur Ukraine-Russia peace efforts
articles.body:
Pope Leo says he hopes Oleshky truce could spur Ukraine-Russia peace efforts
VATICAN CITY – Pope Leo XIV said on Nov 1 that he hoped cooperation between Russia and Ukraine in implementing a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky would pave the way for broader peace efforts.
Ukraine and Russia said on Oct 23 that they had agreed to a ceasefire in Oleshky, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump with the additional involvement of Pope Leo, to allow aid deliveries and evacuations from the front-line town, which has been suffering from acute food and medicine shortages.
“A humanitarian operation has been carried out to help the civilian population in the city of Oleshky. I hope that the cooperation between the parties, which made this necessary humanitarian gesture possible, will strengthen their willingness to engage in dialogue and lead to fresh concrete initiatives for peace,” Pope Leo said during his Sunday prayer.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said peace negotiators would meet for fresh talks in early November.
Pope Leo spoke to both Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky on Oct 16.
Putin told the Pope he supported a Vatican initiative to deliver supplies to civilians in Oleshky and was ready to cooperate, the Kremlin said.
On Oct 27, the Vatican’s foreign minister, Archbishop Paul Gallagher, said that although Leo had recently spoken to Putin and Zelensky, he did not believe the Vatican had played a direct role in arranging the six-day ceasefire. REUTERS

articles.title: Bhutan dedicates Buddhist stupa to PM Modi; Rijiju calls it ‘huge honour’ for India
articles.body:
Union minister Kiren Rijiju during a meeting with Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck during his visit to Gelephu, Bhutan (PTI)
NEW DELHI: Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck has dedicated a sacred Buddhist stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, recognising his contribution to strengthening friendship between the two countries. The dedication of Stupa number 76 took place during a ceremony to raise and consecrate 108 stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City on Sunday.According to news agency ANI, Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju represented India at the ceremony and expressed gratitude to Bhutan for the gesture, describing it as a "huge honour for India". He also conveyed gratitude on behalf of Prime Minister Modi to the Bhutanese King.In a post on X, Rijiju said, "It's a huge honour for India that very sacred stupa 76 is dedicated to Hon'ble PM Narendra Modi ji for his outstanding vision and commitment to friendship between India and Bhutan. On the auspicious occasion of Lhabab Duchen, joined the sacred ceremony in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, marking the raising and consecration of 108 stupas, accompanied by the blowing of Dungchens."He further said, "Paid my respects and offered prayers in the presence of His Majesty the King of Bhutan, Her Majesty the Gyaltsuen, H E Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Prime Minister of Bhutan & the people of Bhutan.
A deeply meaningful spiritual occasion, reflecting Bhutan’s rich Buddhist heritage and the enduring bonds of friendship between our two nations."Stupas are sacred Buddhist structures associated with the teachings and life of Gautama Buddha. Traditionally, they were built to preserve the relics of the Buddha and other revered Buddhist figures, including their ashes and remains. Over time, they became important places of worship, meditation and religious devotion.
The 108 stupas in Bhutan are known as Jangchub Chortens, or Stupas of Enlightenment. The number 108 holds special significance in Buddhist traditions and is associated with religious practices, including the use of 108 beads in prayer malas. The structures are intended to promote peace, harmony and spiritual well-being.Rijiju is visiting Bhutan from October 31 to November 2. Earlier on Sunday, Rijiju met Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay in Gelephu. The two leaders discussed strengthening the India-Bhutan partnership and exploring the potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City project.
Aryan Singh is a journalist with The Times of India, covering breaking news, defence and global conflicts. An alumnus of the IIMC, he tracks the people, weapons and geopolitics behind the headlines, with a focus on India’s national security, military affairs and conflicts shaping the world.

articles.title: Rick Sanchez reports from Alyoshki Russia-Ukraine truce zone (VIDEO)
articles.body:
Rick Sanchez reports from Alyoshki Russia-Ukraine truce zone (VIDEO)
RT’s Rick Sanchez has traveled to the frontline town of Alyoshki in Kherson Region to witness firsthand a rare local ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine aimed at evacuating civilians and delivering humanitarian aid to residents.
An estimated 1,500 to 2,000 people had been trapped in the town on the left bank of the Dnieper River, opposite the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, amid Kiev’s repeated drone strikes and the airdropping of mines on supply roads.
More than 750 civilians have since been evacuated under the six-day truce around Alyoshki, arranged with the assistance of US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV. The ceasefire is set to expire on Sunday evening.
Officials from both sides oversaw the evacuations, with civilians offered the choice of relocating to another city in Russia or traveling to Ukraine via Russia and Belarus. Evacuees and Russian officials interviewed by RT described months of shortages and the hardships of living under shelling they attributed to Ukrainian forces.
The host of Sanchez Effect compared the town’s destruction to that seen during World War II, pointing to what he described as an extraordinarily high concentration of mines of various types scattered throughout the area.
However, Sanchez expressed cautious optimism as he watched Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova work alongside her Ukrainian counterpart, Dmitry Lubinets.
“Could the deal that they worked out for the town of Alyoshki end up being the very thing that sparks some kind of a hopeful sign that maybe both sides can come together in a bigger way?” Sanchez said. He added that some observers believe the truce could pave the way for a broader peace agreement.
Sanchez also suggested that Russia’s drone capabilities may have made Ukraine more willing to “sit down with the Russians.”
Lantratova said she and Lubinets had appealed to Melania Trump to help coordinate further humanitarian missions. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said earlier that, if successful, the Alyoshki truce could serve as a precedent for future agreements.
